objective.statement: Find and write the supertonic chord, ii, including the diminished triad of a minor key.
successCriteria: I build chord ii on the second note of the scale.
I know ii is a minor triad in a major key and a diminished triad in a minor key.
I can name it in any position.

explanation.text: The supertonic is the second note of the scale, and chord ii is the triad built on it. In Grade 5 the chords you identify and write are I, ii, IV and V, in any of the keys you know. The supertonic chord can be in root position or either inversion, like any other.

music.textAlternative: Chord ii of C major: D, F, A from the bottom up.

explanation.caption: ii in C major: D F A, a minor triad (minor 3rd D–F, perfect 5th D–A).

explanation.text: In a major key chord ii is a minor triad. In a minor key it is different: the notes come from the harmonic minor scale, and the triad is built from a minor 3rd and a diminished 5th above the root. This is a diminished triad, shown as ii° in extended Roman numerals (a small circle after a lower-case ii).

music.textAlternative: Chord ii of C minor: D, F, A flat from the bottom up.

explanation.caption: ii° in C minor: D F A♭, with a diminished 5th, D to A♭.

explanation.text: In the exam the numerals are usually printed as capitals (I, II, IV, V); lower case for a minor chord (ii), with the diminished sign if you wish, is also a recognised spelling. The app shows the supertonic as ii: it means the same as II. Inversions of ii work exactly as before: look at the lowest note to find the position.
Chord ii is built on degree 2. Major key: minor triad. Minor key: diminished triad (minor 3rd and diminished 5th).

music.textAlternative: Chord ii of D major: E, G, B from the bottom up.

steps: The second note of D major is E.
Chord ii is E, G, B.
It is in root position: iia.

guided.prompt: Which notes make chord ii (the supertonic triad) of A minor? (Notes are listed from the root upwards.)

D–F–A.reason: That is a chord on a different degree: chord ii is built on the 2nd note of the scale.

E–G♯–B.reason: That is a chord on a different degree: chord ii is built on the 2nd note of the scale.

B–D–F♯.reason: The 5th of chord ii is F: use the notes of the scale (the harmonic minor in a minor key), and the triad is diminished.

hints: Chord ii is built on the second note of the scale.
Chord ii is built on degree 2 of A minor: B. Add the notes a 3rd and a 5th above, taken from the scale.

feedback.correct: Yes: built on the second note.

mistakes.wrong-degree: Chord ii is built on the 2nd degree: its notes come from the scale.
mistakes.root-confused-with-bass: The lowest note isn't always the root. Stack the notes in 3rds to find it, then check the inversion.
mistakes.inversion-misread: Inversion depends on which note of the triad is in the bass: root (a), 3rd (b) or 5th (c).
mistakes.leading-note-not-raised: In minor keys, chords use the harmonic minor, so the leading note is raised.
mistakes.note-missing: One of the notes doesn't belong. A triad has a root, a 3rd and a 5th.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Find the root first, then the bass note.
